subtopic: Arc Length and Area of a Sector
stem: The diameter of a circle is 14 cm. Find the length of the arc, subtending an angle of \(54^\circ\) at the centre.
solution:
Here diameter = 14 cm
\(\therefore\) Radius = \(r\) = 7 cm
\(\theta^{c} = \left(54 \times \frac{\pi}{180}\right)^{c} = \left(\frac{3\pi}{10}\right)^{c}\)
To find s, we know that \(s = r\theta\)
\(= 7 \times \frac{3\pi}{10} = \frac{7 \times 3}{10} \times \frac{22}{7} = \frac{66}{10}\)
\(\therefore\) arc length = 6.6 cm

subtopic: Arc Length and Area of a Sector
stem: In a circle of radius 12 cms, an arc PQ subtends an angle of \(30^\circ\) at the centre. Find the area between the arc PQ and chord PQ.
solution:
[Textbook misprint: the printed solution writes \(\theta^{c} = 30^\circ\), carrying the radian superscript \(c\) on a quantity stated in degrees. Preserved as printed.]

\(r\) = 12 cms,
\(\theta^{c} = 30^\circ = \left(30 \times \frac{\pi}{180}\right)^{c}\)
\(\theta = \left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)^{c}\)
Area of sector OPQ \(= \frac{1}{2} r^{2}\theta = \frac{1}{2} \times 12 \times 12 \times \frac{\pi}{6} = 12\pi\) sq.cm. ...... (1)
Draw QR \(\perp\) OP, \(\therefore \sin 30^\circ = \frac{QR}{12}\)
\(\therefore\) QR \(= 12 \times \frac{1}{2} = 6\) cms = Height of \(\triangle\) OPQ
Area of \(\triangle\) OPQ \(= \frac{1}{2} \times\) base \(\times\) height \(= \frac{1}{2} \times 12 \times 6 = 36\) sq.cm ........(2)
By (1) and (2),
Required Area = A(Sector OPQ) \(-\) A(\(\triangle\)OPQ)
\(= (12\pi - 36)\) sq.cm.
\(= 12(\pi - 3)\) sq.cm
diagramNote: Fig. 1.17: circle centre O with radius 12 to P and Q, central angle POQ = 30 degrees, the segment between chord PQ and arc PQ shaded, and the foot R of the perpendicular QR dropped onto OP. The printed solution names R, which is defined only by the figure.
_note: The book writes the line as "\(\theta^{c} = 30^\circ\)" — a notational slip (the radian superscript c is carried on a quantity stated in degrees). Transcribed as printed.

subtopic: Arc Length and Area of a Sector
stem: The area of a circle is \(225\pi\) sq. cm. Find the length of its arc subtending an angle of \(120^\circ\) at the centre. Also find the area of the corresponding sector.
solution:
Let 'r' be the radius of a circle whose area is \(225\pi\) sq. cm.
\(\therefore \pi r^{2} = 225\pi\)
\(\therefore r^{2} = 225\)
\(\therefore r = 15\) cm.
\(\theta^{c} = 120^\circ = \left(120 \times \frac{\pi}{180}\right)^{c} = \frac{2\pi^{c}}{3}\)
To find s and A.
We know that \(s = r\theta\) and \(A = \frac{1}{2} r^{2}\theta\)
\(\therefore s = 15 \times \frac{2\pi}{3} = 10\pi\) and
\(A = \frac{1}{2} \times 15 \times 15 \times \frac{2\pi}{3} = 75\pi\)
\(\therefore s = 10\pi\) cm and \(A = 75\pi\) sq.cm.

subtopic: Arc Length and Area of a Sector
stem: The perimeter of a sector is equal to half of the circumference of a circle. Find the measure of the angle of the sector at the centre in radian.
solution:
Let \(r\) be the radius of a circle.
Perimeter of a sector = half of the circumference
\(\therefore l(\mathrm{OA}) + l(\mathrm{OB}) + l(\text{arc APB}) = \frac{1}{2}(2\pi r)\)
\(\therefore r + r + r.\theta = \pi r\)
\(2r + r.\theta = \pi r\)
\(\therefore 2 + \theta = \pi\)
\(\therefore \theta = (\pi - 2)^{c}\)
diagramNote: Fig. 1.18: circle centre O with radii OA and OB of length r, central angle AOB = theta, and P a point on the minor arc between B and A so the arc is named APB. The printed solution refers to OA, OB and arc APB, which the figure defines.

subtopic: Arc Length and Area of a Sector
stem: A pendulum of length 21 cm oscillates through an angle of \(36^\circ\). Find the length of its path.
solution:
Here \(r = 21\) cm
\(\theta = 36^\circ = \left(36 \times \frac{\pi}{180}\right)^{c} = \frac{\pi^{c}}{5}\)
Length of its path \(= l(\text{arc AXB})\)
\(= s = r\theta\)
\(= 21 \times \frac{\pi}{5}\)
\(= \frac{21}{5} \times \frac{22}{7} = \frac{66}{5}\)
Length of path = 13.2 cm
diagramNote: Fig. 1.19: a pendulum suspended from a hatched ceiling, the two extreme positions each of length 21 cm making an angle of 36 degrees at the point of suspension, with the swept arc from A to B drawn dotted. The printed solution names arc AXB, whose point X appears only in the figure.

subtopic: Arc Length and Area of a Sector
stem: ABCDEFGH is a regular octagon inscribed in a circle of radius 9 cm. Find the length of minor arc AB.
solution:
Here \(r = 9\) cm.

\(\theta = \frac{360^\circ}{8} = 45^\circ = \left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)^{c}\)

\(l(\text{minor arc AB}) = S = r\theta = 9\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\) cm \(= \frac{9\pi}{4}\) cm.
